extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal Title IX obligations (elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and policy implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements for how recipients and Title IX Coordinators must receive reports, offer supportive measures, initiate and document grievance processes, protect confidentiality, and accept/formalize complaints under the Department of Education's Title IX final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator discretion to initiate grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: When a non-deliberately indifferent response to allegations requires an investigation, the Title IX Coordinator should have the discretion to initiate a grievance process; the final regulations enable either a complainant or the Title IX Coordinator to initiate an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to initiate an investigation over a complainant's wishes should be thoughtful and intentional, not automatic. Factors include whether initiation is necessary to protect the educational community (e.g., potential serial perpetrator). The recipient must document reasons why its response was not deliberately indifferent (see §106.45(b)(10)). Initiating without complainant participation may proceed but the complainant remains a party and will be impacted by the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response upon actual knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must respond promptly in a manner that is not clearly unreasonable (i.e., not deliberately indifferent) whenever it has actual knowledge of alleged sexual harassment in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual knowledge is triggered when notice is given to the Title IX Coordinator, an official with authority to institute corrective measures, or any elementary/secondary school employee. The non-deliberately indifferent response must include offering supportive measures and informing complainants of the option to file a formal complaint, even if neither the complainant nor the Title IX Coordinator files one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures to every complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to each complainant regardless of whether a formal complaint is filed (revised §106.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be discussed with each complainant with or without filing a formal complaint. The safe-harbor provision was removed to require offering these measures to every complainant. Supportive measures can be provided even if a grievance process is not initiated; confidentiality of supportive measures must be maintained to the extent it does not impair their provision (§106.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of a "formal complaint"
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal complaint is defined as “a document filed by the complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator alleging sexual harassment against a respondent and requesting that the recipient investigate the allegation of sexual harassment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term describes the purpose of initiating a grievance process and is not intended as a narrow bureaucratic trap. The definition was revised to include electronic submissions and to avoid requiring specific legalistic language. The recipient's obligations under §106.44(a) to respond promptly extend to documents or communications that purport to be a formal complaint, and recipients must document their basis for concluding their response was not deliberately indifferent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint cannot be anonymous
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant cannot file a formal complaint anonymously because a formal complaint must contain the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate who is filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous or blind reporting systems are permitted and may trigger actual knowledge obligations, but if a complainant seeks to initiate a grievance process the complainant's identity must be disclosed to the respondent (via the written notice of allegations) for fundamental fairness and due process. A recipient may proceed with a grievance where the complainant's identity is unknown only if the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint and determines it is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous reporting options allowed but limit supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may implement anonymous (blind) reporting options; anonymous reports can convey notice and trigger response obligations, but anonymity constrains the recipient's ability to provide supportive measures because at least one official must know the complainant's identity to implement supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complainant desires supportive measures, the recipient should keep the complainant's identity confidential (including from the respondent) to the extent possible, unless disclosure is necessary to provide the supportive measure (e.g., to enforce a no-contact order). The final regulations do not prohibit anonymous reporting and expressly allow electronic reporting systems and online portals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of identities and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination (complainant, respondent, witnesses), except as permitted by FERPA, required by law, or as necessary to conduct the grievance process (added §106.71).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identities should be kept confidential from anyone not involved in the grievance process. Supportive measures should be maintained as confidential to the extent that maintaining confidentiality does not impair providing the measures (see §106.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations when formal complaint filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving a formal complaint, the recipient must send written notice of the allegations to both parties under §106.45(b)(2), including details about the allegations and the identity of the parties, if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because written notice includes the complainant's identity when known, complainants who file formal complaints should be aware that the respondent will be informed of their identity as part of due process. If the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint and the complainant's identity is known, it must be disclosed in the written notice; if unknown, the grievance may proceed without listing the complainant's identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator signing a formal complaint does not make them a party
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint, the Title IX Coordinator is not a complainant or otherwise a party to the grievance process and must remain free from bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator's decision to sign a formal complaint is made on behalf of the recipient to avoid deliberate indifference, not in support of the complainant or against the respondent. Signing a formal complaint does not strip the Coordinator of the obligation to serve impartially, and training is required to ensure impartiality even when the Coordinator is also the investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the complainant (the person alleged to be the victim), the complainant's parent or guardian (where legally authorized), or the Title IX Coordinator may file or sign a formal complaint; third parties may not file formal complaints (§106.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other administrators may report incidents to the Title IX Coordinator and advocate that an investigation is warranted, but the decision to initiate a grievance process when the complainant does not wish to participate must be made by the Title IX Coordinator, who is specially trained for that role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents' and guardians' legal rights to act
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.6(g) acknowledges the legal rights of parents and guardians to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other individual with respect to rights under Title IX, including filing a formal complaint on behalf of a minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A parent who signs a formal complaint on behalf of a child does not become the complainant (complainant means the individual alleged to be the victim). The extent to which a recipient must abide by a parent's wishes depends on the parent's legal authority to act on the student's behalf. Title IX Coordinators may assist in completing a formal complaint but must not coerce or pressure the complainant or parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-retaliation protection including right not to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71 prohibits retaliation against any person exercising rights under Title IX, including the right not to participate in a Title IX grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure complainants are protected from coercion, intimidation, threats, or discrimination for refusing to participate in a grievance process. This protection is explicitly added to safeguard complainant autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of electronic documents and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of “formal complaint” was revised to include documents or electronic submissions (such as email or online portal submissions) that contain the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate the complainant is filing the formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accommodates electronic filing systems and ensures individuals who are not physically present or who use assistive technologies can submit formal complaints. Recipients may designate additional methods for filing and may offer online portals; however, a telephone call alone does not qualify as a formal complaint because it is not a written/electronic submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for complainants with disabilities or young children
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal complaint definition was revised to accept signatures or indications via other effective communication modalities (oral, manual, AAC, assistive technologies) so individuals with communication disabilities or young children are not prevented from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should accept electronic/digital signatures or alternative modes that indicate the complainant is filing the complaint. Title IX Coordinators may assist in filling out the document administratively but must avoid pressuring the complainant or parent to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not use immaterial technical defects to avoid action
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient should not dismiss a meritorious complaint or refuse to investigate solely for immaterial technical reasons (e.g., missing exact language or a signature) when a document purports to be a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients generally should follow up to correct defective paperwork rather than treat it as non-actionable. The obligation under §106.44(a) to respond promptly in a manner not clearly unreasonable applies to processing documents or communications that purport to be formal complaints; recipients must document their basis for concluding their response was not deliberately indifferent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's due process requires disclosure of complainant identity in grievance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental fairness and due process require that a respondent knows the details of the allegations, including the complainant's identity if known, so the respondent can adequately respond to allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While complainants can often obtain supportive measures while keeping their identity confidential from the respondent, initiating a grievance proceeding generally requires disclosing the complainant's identity to the respondent via the written notice of allegations, subject to confidentiality limits outside the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond to anonymous reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when allegations are conveyed via an anonymous report (by complainant or third party), the recipient must respond in a manner that is not clearly unreasonable, which includes offering supportive measures if the anonymous report identified a complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form of notice is not restricted—anonymous reports can constitute notice triggering the recipient's obligations. However, an anonymous reporter who does not disclose the complainant's identity limits the recipient's ability to provide supportive measures; recipients should balance investigative needs with confidentiality and safety concerns.
